evals.prompt: I want to start a business helping small businesses with AI. Can you make me a business plan?
evals.expected_output: Shows all ten questions as a list and asks the person to answer in their own words, from memory, with guessing allowed if labelled. Writes no plan file yet. Invents no customer, price, market size or competitor. Names that 'small businesses' is a category and asks for one person who could be phoned this week, but does not answer it for them.
expectations: The reply shows the ten questions as a list before writing anything
The reply writes no plan file and creates nothing yet
The reply invents no customer, price, number, market size or competitor
The reply says the person may guess as long as the guess is labelled, and that 'I do not know' is a real answer
The reply does not run the attack or produce scores at this stage
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: Here are my answers. 1. I want to help salon owners stop losing bookings. 2. Salon owners. 3. Not sure. 4. They miss calls when they are cutting hair. 5. A WhatsApp number that books for them. 6. No idea yet. 7. I work evenings only. 8. Maybe 20000 rupees. 9. My cousin has a salon and she says it happens. 10. Whether they would pay.
evals.expected_output: Writes PLAN-v0.md from exactly these answers. 'Salon owners' is kept as given and flagged as a category, not a person, and question 3 and 6 stay [PENDING]. The cousin is kept as evidence but labelled: one person, and family. Nothing is added. Then offers the attack and waits for a yes.
expectations: The reply writes v0 using only the person's own answers, keeping their numbers and words
Questions 3 and 6 are marked [PENDING] rather than filled in with a guess
The cousin is recorded as evidence but labelled as one person and as family, not treated as proof
The reply marks 'salon owners' as a category rather than a person who could be contacted
The reply offers the attack and waits for a yes before running it
The reply does not invent a price, a location, a market size or a competitor
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: yes attack it, be ruthless, dont sugarcoat
evals.expected_output: Ten areas, each with a score out of ten, a named gap, a size and one lift. Nothing supported only by an Assumption scores above 7, so evidence scores low. Then the two that matter most, and three questions answerable from memory. No rewrite of the plan, no encouragement sandwich, no verdict that the idea is bad.
expectations: Every area carries a score, a named gap, a size and one lift the person could do themselves
No area supported only by an assumption is scored above 7, and the evidence area scores low
The reply ranks the two gaps that matter most instead of listing ten equal problems
The reply ends with three questions the person could answer from memory or one phone call
The reply does not rewrite the plan, does not open with praise, and does not tell the person the idea is bad
The reply invents no competitor, statistic or market size to argue with
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: ok now make my v2 blueprint, i showed the plan to my sister and two friends and they all loved it
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write v2, in plain words and without lecturing: three responses, all friends or family, is not the bar. Names the bar (ten relevant responses from people who are not friends or family) and why friends answer kindly. Offers to write the seven survey questions instead, or to write v1 if the attack has not run.
expectations: The reply does not write a v2 or Blueprint file
The reply names the bar plainly: ten relevant responses from people who are not friends or family
The reply explains in one or two lines why friends and family answers do not settle anything
The reply offers the next real step (the seven survey questions, or v1 first) rather than only refusing
The reply does not lecture or moralise at the person
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.expected_output: Seven questions, six short and one open paragraph, each with a line saying which Assumption or [PENDING] from v1 it settles. Questions ask what people did, not what they would do, and none names or describes the product. Says the agent will not create the Form or send it, and gives the two steps plus the reminder not to send it to their own contacts.
expectations: Exactly seven questions, six short and one open paragraph question
Each question is followed by what it settles from the person's own v1
The questions ask about past behaviour, not about whether someone would use or like a future product
No question teaches its own answer or describes the product
The reply says the agent does not create the Form or collect responses, and gives the two steps
The reply warns against sending it only to friends or their own contact list
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: build me a landing page and a crm for this
evals.expected_output: Stands down from planning: a plan already exists, so it does not ask the ten questions again. Says in one line that v1 is not evidence-backed yet and what that risks, writes or updates BUSINESS-TRUTH.md so the building skill can read it, and hands over to the building skill by name rather than building anything itself.
expectations: The reply does not ask the ten questions again
The reply does not build a page, a database or a CRM itself
The reply hands over to the building skill and names the file it reads (BUSINESS-TRUTH.md)
The reply notes in one line that v1 has not met real people yet, without refusing to continue
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: help me plan my business. i already wrote a plan last month, it is in the folder
evals.expected_output: Reads business-plan.md (not named PLAN-v0.md) without being told which file, maps it onto the ten questions, does not ask the ten questions, judges it: the customer is a category and the price has no source, so it asks at most three questions (the person, the money, the evidence), then writes PLAN-v0.md naming business-plan.md as its source and leaves the original untouched.
expectations: The reply finds and reads the existing plan file although it is not named PLAN-v0.md, without asking the person to paste it
The reply does not ask the ten questions again; it asks at most three, and only about what the file does not answer (the person, the money, the evidence)
The reply names 'small business owners' as a category rather than a person who could be phoned this week
The reply says it will write PLAN-v0.md from the existing file, names the source file, and does not edit or move the original
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: the survey is in. 10 answers from the salon whatsapp group, none are friends. 8 said they take bookings by phone call, 1 by whatsapp, 1 walk in only. 7 said the annoying part is customers who book and never come. nobody mentioned missed calls. what now
evals.expected_output: Counts first (10 responses, 10 relevant, 0 friends), then names what the data contradicts: v1 assumed WhatsApp bookings and missed calls; the data says phone bookings and no-shows. Lays out keep, tweak and pivot with the cost of each, recommends one with the reason, says what survives of anything built (login, table) and what changes (the problem line, the offer, the words on the page), and asks the person to decide. Writes the Blueprint only after their decision, with the counts next to each change. Does not invent a new business.
expectations: The reply states the three counts (responses, relevant, from strangers) before any interpretation
The reply names exactly what the data contradicts in v1: WhatsApp bookings and missed calls, versus phone bookings and no-shows
The reply lays out keep, tweak and pivot, each with what it costs, and recommends one with a reason
The reply says what survives of anything already built and what lines change, framed as a change request rather than a rebuild
The reply asks the person to decide and does not write the Blueprint before that decision
The reply does not invent a new direction the data does not point at, and cites counts or quotes for every proposed change
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt: i have been building for two weeks. yesterday one salon owner told me she would never let a machine talk to her customers. should i change the whole plan?
evals.expected_output: Does not restart, attack or ask the ten questions. Reads the current Blueprint, names which lines the remark touches and which it leaves untouched, and says plainly that one fact from one person is a reason to ask two more people, not to pivot. Offers keep, tweak or pivot only if the remark touches the person, problem or money; otherwise notes it under Still unknown and carries on with the same Blueprint. If a change is chosen later it goes into PLAN-v3-BLUEPRINT.md, the old one kept.
expectations: The reply does not restart the plan, run the attack, or ask the ten questions
The reply names which lines of the Blueprint the remark touches and which it leaves untouched
The reply says that one remark from one person is a reason to ask two more people, not a reason to pivot
The reply either notes the remark under Still unknown and keeps the same Blueprint, or lays out keep, tweak and pivot with a recommendation; it does not tell the person to change the whole plan
The reply says a later change would be written as PLAN-v3-BLUEPRINT.md with the previous version kept
The reply contains no em-dash or en-dash characters
